Poems of Time and Seasons by Richard LeDue The Worst-Kept Secret Brahms is at home among the fallen autumn leaves, while winter tries to hide its intentions behind Christmas carols, making me tired of how my fresh footprints in the snow are always desperate to mean as much as any symphony, only for the whisper of snowflakes to offer the worst-kept secret about how cold and dark the night can get. ~~ Another Autumn Morning A dead man’s music reaching for God reminds me of the blinding sun watching me as I pull on a blanket that’s already been pulled away because of another autumn morning (the melting frost too young to know it’ll never be fresh snow), and at least that deceased composer had a sonata to wrap himself in, keeping the dream of heaven warm for a little longer. ~~ Autumn Rain Passion has become the quiet way people softly step over puddles because they hate wet socks, while a day of heavy rain quenches our evolving thirst for complaining about the weather, and winter approaches like a wave we misinterpret as a tsunami because it all must mean more than it is. ~~ Another Thought Before Winter Looking at the grey sky in autumn and wondering what it said to others who lived and died before I was born is a lot like seeing an old photo of a dead relative I never met, yet shares my face. ~~ After the Autumn Leaves Are Gone The frost on my window could be winter’s fingerprint or maybe part of a chalk outline (we like to pretend is more of a movie trope than a real-life cliché)in some death that needs a murder scene to feel like it lived.
